title: Remove empty-root credits from the paired BIT supplier at 0.00385248 (no new κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Remove empty-body root credits from the existing BIT dependency while preserving ordinary saving **0.00385248**. **No new κ.** Two actual 111-port native calls at each of 18 stages supply 111 paired QUERY-only chains. The 798-event caller has 38 independent inputs, no QSELF and no rank-one productive credit.

The complete identity is Tnew = 2 Told - 222 H1 and Pnew = 2 Pold - 222 H1: the signed moment and #6834's crossing are preserved, not improved. The fixed odd-port determinant obstruction explains why one unpaired copy cannot meet this target contract. The bootstrap starts from selected BIT .0034, then .0038507 and .00385248, without reusing the old empty-credit supplier.

## Sources and verification

Base: `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`. Extends #6980's QUERY-only caller and #6834's chain-root accounting; #6726 remains native provenance only. Full commit/path/blob/SHA256 pins are in INPUT-PINS.json.

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/paired-query-only-bit
```

Expected registered PASS and `PASS_PAIRED_EFREE_BIT_EXISTING_00385248`. Main and separate reverse/operator/interval checks passed; optimized primary replay also passed. Checks cover all 1,444 caller coefficients in each direction, the exact retained native, 36 calls, 19,950 targets and 107,352 paid jobs. Complete ordinary work is 741,106,511,760 < 10^12; owned reserve is 6,878,988 < 10^7. Controls reject omitted calls, QUERY without q, an identity root target and illegal division after characteristic-two specialization.

## Limits and credit

The native, owned, compiler, precision/tape and analytic contracts remain. No physical all-width admission, accepted-frontier update or unconditional multiplier is claimed. Genuine sharing between paired native copies remains open. Optional full-history preflight was unavailable in the deliberately shallow checkout; byte authentication and committed-tree checks passed.

Prepared for **@CubeJerry**, with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance**, including separate implementations for independent checks. Credit DreamingOfClouds, zxv, Ali Romman, Cinna Davis and the retained authors; model-assisted review is not human acceptance.
